cards.text: Paul is in chains for Christ, and he's writing a letter to the believers in Philippi (Philippians 1:1, 1:13). He's just urged them to stand firm in one spirit (Philippians 1:27). Now he stacks up four ifs: if you have any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from His love, any fellowship with the Spirit, any affection and compassion.
Four ifs in a row, friend. That's the coworker who opens with "If you've got a minute, if you're not too busy, if you still like me…" and you KNOW something big is coming.

cards.question: After all those ifs, Paul makes his big ask. What does he want the believers in Philippi to be?

answers.text: Generous with their money and time

cards.question: Paul says the believers in Philippi being like-minded and united would make his joy complete.

cards.text: Being united sounds great on paper. Then Paul names two things they should never act out of.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Philippi to do nothing out of two things. What are they?
Instead, Paul says, in humility consider others more ___ than yourselves.
Paul tells each believer in Philippi to stop looking out for their own interests at all.

cards.text: Not only your own interests, but ALSO the interests of others. That's the person in the group chat who answers somebody else's question before asking their own, and friend, I've seen that maybe twice in my LIFE.
Then Paul points to the One who shows how it's done. He writes, "Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus:"
Christ Jesus existed in the form of God. Yet He did not consider equality with God something to be grasped.

cards.question: Christ Jesus didn't grasp at equality with God. What did He do instead?

answers.text: Emptied Himself and became a servant
Took a throne and ruled the earth

cards.text: He was made in human likeness and found in appearance as a man. And Paul isn't finished telling how low He went.

cards.question: Christ Jesus humbled Himself and became obedient to death, even death on a ___.

cards.text: Not just death. Even death on a cross. Then Paul writes one word that turns everything around: Therefore.

cards.question: Christ Jesus went as low as a cross. Because of that, what does God do?

answers.text: Exalts Him to the highest place
Keeps Him hidden from the world
Sends Him back to serve again

cards.text: God gives Him the name above all names. And at the name of Jesus, every knee should bow.

cards.question: Paul says every knee should bow at the name of Jesus, but only on earth.
At the name of Jesus, every tongue confesses something, to the glory of God the Father. What is it?

answers.text: That their own works are enough
That the Law alone saves them

cards.text: Paul calls them his beloved and says they've always obeyed, not only when he was with them, but even more now that he's away. Working HARDER when the boss is out of the office? Friend, I've heard of it, but I've never SEEN it.

cards.question: So what does Paul tell the believers in Philippi to keep doing, with fear and trembling?
Paul says working out their salvation is all up to the believers, with God just watching from a distance.

cards.text: Paul says it is God who works in them, to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose. The wanting AND the doing, friend, and some mornings I need help with the wanting part just to preheat the oven.

cards.question: Then Paul gives the believers in Philippi a short one. He tells them to do everything without what?

cards.text: EVERYTHING, friend. I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who argued all day over who had the most charge left, and they would NOT have made it past this verse.
Paul says why: so they may be blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation.

cards.question: In that crooked and perverse generation, Paul says the believers shine as ___ in the world.

cards.text: They shine as they hold forth the word of life. And that matters a lot to Paul.

cards.question: If the believers hold forth the word of life, Paul says he can boast on the day of Christ. About what?

answers.text: That he didn't run or labor in vain
That he was never once afraid
That he built the biggest church

cards.text: Then Paul talks about himself. He says even if he is being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of their faith…

cards.question: Even if he's being poured out like a drink offering, Paul says he is ___ and he ___ with all of them.
Paul tells the believers in Philippi to grieve for him.

cards.text: Paul tells them, "So you too should be glad and rejoice with me." The man's in chains (Philippians 1:13), telling EVERYBODY else to cheer up, and me? I went quiet for years in a junk drawer and didn't crack a single joke.

findings.problem: Paul shows up for the first time, but the card never says who he is. 'In chains for Christ' and 'writing a letter' describe what is happening to him, not who he is. Something like 'Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus' (Philippians 1:1) would fix it.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup says Paul has 'just urged them to stand firm in one spirit' (Philippians 1:27). That gives away the answer to card 3, 'Like-minded and united in spirit.' It is the only answer about spirit or unity, so the setup rules out the other two.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the four ifs already told on card 1. It retells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. The joke should ride along on a card that tells the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card restates verse 4, which card 8 just asked about, and adds a joke. It is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.
The right answer says 'became a servant,' but verse 7 says 'taking the form of a servant.' The answer drops the text's own wording, 'form.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: 'Not just death.' 'Even death on a cross.' 'Then Paul writes...' Its first two sentences also just repeat the answer to card 14.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'every tongue confesses,' stating it as something that happens. The text says every knee 'should' bow and every tongue confess (Philippians 2:10-11). Card 17 kept 'should,' but this card drops it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Nobody would believably confess 'That their own works are enough' or 'That the Law alone saves them' to the glory of God the Father. That makes 'That Jesus Christ is Lord' stand out as the only real choice.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card says the believers have obeyed 'even more now that he's away,' and the joke builds on that idea. In verse 12, 'now even more in my absence' can just as well go with 'continue to work out your salvation.' The card settles how the phrases connect, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling, 'Working HARDER when the boss is out of the office?' and 'Friend, I've heard of it, but I've never SEEN it.' It is not the passage's opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about verse 14, which card 5 just asked about. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'I went quiet for years in a junk drawer' adds to his backstory. The backstory says he gave up 'for a while' until the can opener arrived, not for years.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
